item.title: Next Michigan AD: 'It depends' on coach-student sexual relationships
item.description: Trev Alberts , who is expected to be named the University of Michigan's next athletic director, said "it depends" when asked during a December deposition whether college coaches should ever have sexual relationships with student-athletes , despite a University of Nebraska-Lincoln policy prohibiting such relationships. Alberts gave the testimony during the deposition as a defendant in an ongoing federal lawsuit alleging that he and other University of Nebraska-Lincoln officials mishandled a sexual relationship between an associate women's basketball coach and a player during his tenure as athletic director. The lawsuit was filed by Ashley Scoggin, a former Nebraska women's basketball player. She claimed the university didn't protect her and failed to properly investigate how she, as a student-athlete, was "groomed" by associate women's basketball coach Chuck Love to carry on a secret relationship. Alberts is named as a defendant, along with head coach Amy Williams, Love and Nebraska's Board of Regents. In a response to Scoggin's lawsuit, attorneys for Williams, Alberts and the university denied her allegations and said the defendants were unaware of the details of the relationship until she filed a Title IX complaint in March 2022. The lawsuit also alleges Alberts failed to question Williams' decision to remove Scoggin from the team or investigate whether Love had relationships with other students and whether Williams knew about them. It further alleges he failed to require employee training or clarify athletic department policies prohibiting sexual relationships between coaches and student-athletes. The lawsuit also alleges Alberts encouraged Scoggin to leave Nebraska and allowed Love to resign voluntarily. Attorneys for Scoggin declined to comment. Messages were left with Alberts and attorneys for him and the university. Nebraska's Senior Director of Communications Cara Pesek declined to comment and said the university did not comment on pending litigation. More: Trev Alberts set to become next UM athletic director Expert questions Alberts' comments as Michigan faces scrutiny Nellie Drew, the director of the Center for the Advancement of Sport at the University at Buffalo School of Law, said Alberts' comments were "flabbergasting." Understanding the university's and federal government's policies regarding Title IX and sexual harassment are a "core component" of an athletic director's job, she said. "There's a difference between not being aware of something happening and not being aware of what you need to be doing as a mandatory reporter," Drew said. "He was (at the Nebraska system) for a long time, should’ve been doing mandatory training. ... He signs off on annual affirmations that the university is in compliance." item.title: Philadelphia Eagles Finally Get Good News Before Steelers Game
item.description: It has been an absolutely miserable NFL season for the Philadelphia Eagles, and at no point have things been looking up. The Eagles are just 2-7 heading into their Week 11 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Jalen Hurts is out for the season. They traded multiple key pieces before the trade deadline. Their receiving corps have also been riddled with injuries. But in terms of the latter, Philadelphia has finally received some good news. Both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks were in practice this week, and Smith particular has been given the green light to play this Sunday against the Steelers, per the team’s injury report . Smith last played on Oct. 18 due to a hamstring injury. In the four games he has played this season, he has logged 26 catches for 310 yards and a couple of touchdowns. Where do the Philadelphia Eagles go from here? Oct 18, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith (6) walks off the field after a loss against the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Eagles appear to be entering a rebuilding phase, and their future is definitely up in the air. On the bright side, Philadelphia has stockpiled draft capital thanks to the recent trades it has made. Philly moved center Cam Jurgens and defensive tackle Jordan Davis prior to the deadline. And last June, it sent wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots. That obviously puts the Eagles in a strong position moving forward, especially with general manager Howie Roseman at the helm. But with Hurts’ future very much uncertain due to blood clots, Philadelphia may have to consider making a change under center in the spring, so it will be interesting to see how the Eagles approach it. For now, though, there is now question that Philadelphia is no longer a legitimate contender and will definitely have to retool in order to re-establish itself as a serious threat in the NFC East. item.title: Vikings Receive Sudden Injury News Before 49ers Game
item.description: The Minnesota Vikings have been dealing with a whole lot of injury issues recently, and now, another problem has surfaced before their Week 11 matchup with the San Francisco 49ers. Vikings cornerback Isaiah Rodgers, who has developed into a crucial part of the team’s secondary, is now questionable to play this Sunday as a result of a calf injury that limited him in practice both Thursday and Friday. The development was revealed by Minnesota head coach Kevin O’Connell while speaking to reporters on Friday. O’Connell certainly didn’t seem overly pessimistic, but Rodgers’ condition is obviously something to monitor heading into the Vikings’ showdown in Mexico City. “He was limited today. Minnesota acquired Cousins before the NFL trade deadline, bringing him back for his second stint in the Twin Cities. He initially played for the Vikings between 2018 and 2023, but failed to lead the Vikings to a Super Bowl appearance. That could certainly change this year, as Minnesota boasts a dominant defense and a plethora of weapons offensively. item.title: Greinke And Hosmer Join Royals Hall Of Fame For 2027 Class
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Kansas City Royals have chosen two familiar faces for their 2027 Hall of Fame class. The team made the announcement to mark their lasting impact on the franchise. In the 2002 MLB Draft, Greinke was selected sixth overall. He made his debut in 2004 and pitched for the team until 2010. After a long career with other teams, he returned for his final two seasons in 2022 and 2023. His time in Kansas City included a Cy Young Award win in 2009, according to Royals Keep . He remains the most recent Royals pitcher to earn that title. A Pitcher’s Legacy in the Majors Greinke’s stats show his value to the team over many years. He ranks fourth in club history for strikeouts and sixth in starts. During his career, he earned six All-Star appearances and six Gold Glove Awards. He also won two Silver Slugger Awards while playing for the Dodgers, Angels, Astros and Diamondbacks. His return to the rotation in 2022 helped close out his career in the city where it began. The 2009 season stands out as a peak moment for the franchise. Greinke became the third Royals pitcher to win the Cy Young Award. David Cone won it in 1994 and Bret Saberhagen won it in 1985 and 1989. His ability to dominate hitters made him a key figure for years. Hosmer and the World Series Win Hosmer was the third overall pick in the 2008 draft. He debuted in 2011 and spent his first seven years in Kansas City. His defense at first base earned him four Gold Glove awards. He also won an All-Star Game MVP in 2016 and a Silver Slugger Award in 2017. The 2015 World Series remains the crowning achievement of his time with the Royals. Hosmer played a vital part in the team’s title run against the New York Mets. He scored the game-tying run in the clinching game to propel the team to victory. The game-tying run helped the Royals win their first championship since 1985. His contribution was instrumental in securing the trophy. Despite playing elsewhere, his roots in Kansas City run deep. The team recognized his role in the 2014 and 2015 World Series appearances. His legacy includes the excitement of those playoff runs. Induction Marks a New Chapter The announcement came from the team with a clear statement of pride. “We are proud to announce the newest inductees into the Royals Hall of Fame, Zack Greinke and Eric Hosmer!” the Kansas City Royals said. Greinke and Hosmer each played significant roles in Royals history. Their careers spanned the team’s pitching peak and its championship glory. Royals fans hold the two forever indebted in their hearts. The 2027 class will join the ranks of legends who shaped the game in Kansas City.

item.description: Gerwyn Price won the last of his three Grand Slam of Darts titles in 2021 [Getty Images] Gerwyn Price faced two match darts before winning a thrilling quarter-final against Nico Springer at the Grand Slam of Darts, as Luke Littler's conqueror Jermaine Wattimena was knocked out. Three-time champion Price led for most of the match but his German opponent refused to let him out of reach. Springer missed a number of chances to level, including three darts at double top to make it 13-13 as he fell 14-12 behind, before he eventually made it 14-14 and then took a 15-14 lead. However, Price produced a stunning 143 checkout to take it to a decider in which Springer had the throw. The German left himself 73 after his 16th 180, only to miss double eight and double four for the match prior to Price taking out 78 with treble 18 and double 12. "I'm quite lucky to come through that game," Price told Sky Sports. "I missed so many chances - I should've punished him. "I kept him in the game, I kept missing doubles after doubles. Even though he was scoring as well as I was, I was missing opportunities after opportunities but I'm glad I had another one at the end." Grand Slam of Darts: Schedule, results & prize money Price will play Kevin Doets in the semi-finals after the Dutchman beat compatriot Wattimena, who beat world number one and world champion Littler in the second round. Doets was 5-4 down before taking a dominant hold of the match with a remarkable 10-leg burst. He hit two 170 checkouts as he surged into a 14-5 lead before Wattimena managed to temporarily halt him by taking the 20th leg. However, Doets quickly went on to wrap up victory as he finished off the 23rd leg with a 180 - his eighth of the match - and double 18. "The beginning was very tight but, after the 5-5, I just felt like I was walking away with it," said Doets. When talking about his 170 finishes, he added: "It's amazing to do that - it feels really good to do that." But, that doesn't mean they're not going to make moves. This offseason, the Dodgers could look for some infield help, and that's exactly the move they've reportedly just made a week before Thanksgiving. Dodgers reportedly acquire Royce Lewis from Twins "Royce Lewis traded to Dodgers," Heyman reported Friday afternoon. The move for the Dodgers is not yet official, but it's a fascinating addition for Los Angeles this offseason. With Miguel Rojas retiring this offseason, the Dodgers needed a versatile infielder who is also a right-handed hitter. That's exactly what Lewis is, and he's now on his way to Los Angeles. Lewis, the 27-year-old former No. 1 overall pick back in the 2017 MLB Draft, is coming off his fifth season playing in the Majors, all with the Twins. item.title: When John Madden was the Raiders’ ‘Unknown Coach’
item.description: Editor’s note: This story first appeared in the November 1976 issue of SPORT magazine, written by Wells Twombly. Two months later, John Madden’s Raiders beat the Minnesota Vikings in Super Bowl XI. He went on to become a Hall of Fame coach, the defining voice of NFL broadcasts and the name on the best-selling football video game ever made. In 1976, SPORT still called him the Raiders’ “unknown coach.” Founded in 1946, eight years before Sports Illustrated, SPORT was America’s first national sports magazine. Through a partnership with SPORT magazine , The Sporting Tribune republishes a classic story and photos from the magazine’s archive each month. Who's That Guy Standing Next To The Oakland Raiders? IT'S THEIR UNKNOWN COACH, JOHN MADDEN.... By Wells Twombly When you consider the man's distinctive physical appearance and his joyous, flamboyant personality, it is all the more amazing that so few people have heard of John Madden of the Oakland Raiders. He is almost impossible to avoid, stomping the sidelines on an autumn after-noon, his large face flaming red, shouting and accusing as if someone was about to burn his house and slaughter his family. And he is the most successful unknown coach in the world. Madden simply does not register on the average person's mental screen. Try this simple test on your friends. Back them up against the bar after a long day's work and ask them to identify the only coach who ever won 70 games his first seven years in the National Football League. Or ask: Who has coached six division champions in the past seven years? Or: Who has produced more winning streaks of five games or better than any other active coach? John Madden, at age 40, has accomplished more sooner and received less credit for it than any other coach or manager you can name. All Madden does is win games. But the one game he doesn't win is the Super Bowl — and he works for Al Davis, a club owner so overpowering that he blots out the sun. So John Madden remains an individual waiting to be discovered. "Right off, I'd say that Madden is one of the finest young coaches around," says Paul Brown of the Cincinnati Bengals. "Rarely does he go into a game with only one way to beat you. Sometimes he has three, four or five. The man is a real thinker. He's a real intellectual." Madden has been described by one of his former players, defensive tackle Tom Keating, as "sweaty, like an Irish bartender on a milltown Saturday night." Photographers have won prizes taking his picture during games. One such picture leaps out at you from the wall of the lounge at the Pro Football Hall of Fame in Canton, Ohio. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
